title: Crème de châtaignes
subtitle: Smooth chestnut cream soup
excerpt: Velvety autumn soup made from cooked chestnuts simmered with onion, celery, and stock, blended until smooth, and finished with cream. Earthy, lightly sweet, and deeply seasonal.
sourceNotes: Chestnut soups appear throughout the culinary traditions of the Ardèche, Corrèze, and other chestnut-growing regions of France. The dish is documented in regional French cooking references and broader French culinary encyclopaedias including Larousse Gastronomique (1938). Vacuum-packed cooked chestnuts make it a practical year-round recipe.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the cream. Defrost, reheat, and add cream to finish.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made a day ahead and refrigerated. Reheat gently before serving.

content.text: Crème de châtaignes is one of the most comforting soups of the French autumn. Chestnuts have an earthy sweetness that needs very little help: a softened onion, a stick of celery, good stock, cream. The soup blends down into something the colour of café au lait, and serves as a first course that is properly seasonal. Vacuum-packed cooked chestnuts mean you do not need to spend an hour peeling them.

items.prepNote: vacuum-packed cooked chestnuts, or fresh roasted and peeled

content.text: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and celery and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until completely soft. Add the thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chestnuts and stir to coat. Pour in the hot stock. Bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes until the chestnuts are very soft. Remove the thyme sprigs.
Blend the soup until completely smooth. Return to the pan over gentle heat. Stir in the double cream. Season with salt and pepper. Taste and adjust.

items.symptom: Soup is gluey rather than silky
items.cause: Too many chestnuts relative to stock
items.fix: Add more hot stock, 100 ml at a time, until the soup flows smoothly off a spoon.

items.cause: Chestnuts are naturally sweet; no savoury balance
items.fix: Season assertively with salt and pepper. A very small amount of cider vinegar or lemon juice, added carefully, cuts the sweetness.

content.text: Chestnut soup is the food of the Ardèche and the Corrèze: departments in the Massif Central where chestnut trees once provided a staple carbohydrate for the rural population. The October chestnut harvest remains a major local event, and crème de châtaignes is the soup you find in farmhouse auberges from late September onwards. Topped with a swirl of cream, a few roasted chestnut pieces, and a sprig of thyme, it is one of the prettiest autumnal first courses.
